newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan tea prices seen to have peaked.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan tea prices seen to have peaked.

text.p: Sri Lankan tea prices were firm to slightly lower at the Colombo auction on Wednesday after the weekly average price hit a new record last week, brokers said.

"The market was good contrary to expectations. Barring the poorer type of teas all other types ended firm," said a broker at Eastern Brokers. "Because of increasing quantities ahead the market is expected to come down a little."

The estimated auction average price for the 4.9 million kg on offer fell to 122 rupees per kg from last week's all time high of 124.08 rupees, which surpassed the previous week's record 123.71 rupees, brokers Forbes and Walker said.
Brokers said they originally expected the market to drop last week because buyers were seen holding back in anticipation of bigger volumes in the coming auctions.
"The market seems to have peaked," said the broker from Eastern Brokers. "I don't think the auction average will go beyond this."
Tea prices have been soaring in recent weeks because of higher demand and lower quantities.
The next auction is on October 29-30 where 5.3 million kg will be on offer.
